description: Context-decoupled structural demux baseline. A deterministic parser keeps tag syntax in a skeleton stream, moves non-tag alphabetic prose runs into a prose stream, moves digit runs into a numeric stream, compresses streams independently with LZMA2, and falls back to raw LZMA2 when demux loses.
hypothesis: Separate syntax/prose/numeric distributions before backend coding so XML and MediaWiki structure do not shatter prose contexts.
score_rule: S = compressed archive bytes + counted program bytes.
verdict: Block demux proves a real archive win on 10MB, but counted Python source makes it a scored loss versus tiny raw-LZMA wrappers. Word-level demux is pruned because marker overhead dominates.
